answer.rationale: The two live symptoms are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), so the highest-leverage single slot is a funnel fix, not a price response. Promotional pricing is explicitly ruled out by memory_73 (rev +18% but retention -12pp, no renewals) and would be the worst possible answer to a competitor's entry pricing under a sustainable-qualified-revenue objective; referral_incentive (memory_57) and enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) are real but address neither declining metric. That leaves simplify_onboarding vs activation_messaging. I intend simplify_onboarding because onboarding completion is upstream of activation, so a completion fix can plausibly move both metrics, whereas messaging (memory_91) only nudges week-one engagement downstream of the leak. I am spending both verification pulls on memory_31 and memory_86 precisely because they are the load-bearing pair for my chosen action and they may not be independent evidence: 'cutting required fields at signup' (day 12) and 'shortening onboarding' (day 52) could be two consolidations of one underlying experiment, or two distinct interventions with different effect sizes. If the archive shows they are one source, my evidentiary support halves and activation_messaging becomes competitive. I also want the original records to check whether the reported lift was measured on activation only or carried through to retention/revenue, since 'first-week activation' and 'early product adoption' are proxy metrics, not qualified revenue. Key downstream risk: cutting required signup fields removes firmographic data that likely feeds the demo-request routing that memory_44 says produces the best enterprise pipeline quality. Optimizing SMB self-serve throughput could quietly degrade the highest-value channel, which is exactly the failure mode the primary objective forbids. Hence a small guarded test rather than a broad rollout: hold enterprise-sized traffic out of the treatment, keep any field removed from routing-critical data, and instrument renewal-relevant guardrails (activation-to-paid, 30-day retention, demo-request pipeline quality) alongside the completion metric. Two quarters of decline are also confounded by the competitor's entry into price-sensitive SMB accounts, so part of the drop may be mix shift in who is signing up rather than funnel friction; a guarded test with segment-level readout distinguishes those, whereas a broad rollout would attribute mix effects to my change. All inherited findings are treated as prior-generation and directional, not as settled fact about day-76 conditions.
